audio.t: Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to the Service-Learning Center orientation. I'm Grace Wu, the program coordinator. As you know, every undergraduate needs to complete thirty-six hours of service before graduation, but this semester we're making a few changes. First, hours from one-time events, like a single beach cleanup, will now count for no more than twelve of your total hours. We want you to build a real relationship with one partner organization, so most of your hours should come from a long-term placement.

Our partners this year include a senior care center, two rural elementary schools that need online English tutors, and a local animal shelter. Before you start, you must attend a two-hour training session and sign a safety agreement. At the end of the semester, you'll write a short reflection, and your supervisor will fill out an evaluation form. Only when both are submitted will your hours be officially recorded. If you have any questions, my office hours are Tuesday and Thursday afternoons.

questions.explain: 講者自我介紹 I'm Grace Wu, the program coordinator，選 A。安養中心只是合作單位之一，並非講者身分。
options: A nurse at a senior care center

questions.explain: 講者說單次活動的時數 no more than twelve，即有上限，選 B。總時數仍是三十六小時（A 錯）；訓練是 must attend（C 錯）。
options: Students need more total service hours
One-time events can count for only a limited number of hours

head: From: Kevin Chou, Volunteer Coordinator, Hope Senior Care Center
To: Student Volunteers, Fall Semester
Subject: Schedule update and reminders
passage: Thank you for your hard work this semester. Our residents look forward to your Wednesday visits, and several family members have told us how much they appreciate the conversation and music sessions you lead.

Starting November 18, our Wednesday afternoon session will begin at 2:30 instead of 2:00, because the residents' physical therapy schedule has been extended. The session will still last 90 minutes. If the new time conflicts with your classes, please let me know by November 13 so I can arrange an **alternative** shift on Saturday morning.

Also, a reminder: please do not bring outside food for residents, as many of them follow strict diets. Instead, feel free to bring board games, photos, or musical instruments. Finally, remember to sign in at the front desk on every visit. Your sign-in record is what we use to confirm your service hours with your university.

questions.explain: 信中說 because the residents' physical therapy schedule has been extended，物理治療時間延長，選 B。週六反而是提供的替代班次（D 錯）。
options: The residents' therapy now takes longer
The front desk is closed until 2:30
questions.prompt: Why is the Wednesday session changing?

questions.explain: 若新時間與課衝堂，可改排週六的班，alternative 指「替代的」，最接近 substitute，選 C。並非額外加班（additional）。
questions.prompt: The word "alternative" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to

questions.explain: 信中說 please do not bring outside food for residents，因許多長輩有飲食限制，選 D。樂器與照片是鼓勵攜帶的，簽到則是必須做的。
options: Sign in at the front desk

passage: When Riverside University introduced its service-learning requirement ten years ago, many students saw it as just another box to check. Undergraduates had to complete 36 hours of community service before graduation, and most simply collected hours wherever they could find them: a beach cleanup one weekend, a charity concert the next.

According to a survey released last month by the university's Service-Learning Center, that attitude is changing. Of the 1,200 students who responded, 64 percent said they had stayed with the same partner organization for at least one full semester, up from just 28 percent five years ago. More than half said their service experience had influenced their choice of major or career plans.

Center director Dr. Helen Tsai credits two policy changes. Three years ago, the university began limiting the number of hours students could earn from one-time events. It also added a required reflection report, in which students connect their service to what they learn in class. "When students have to explain what they learned, they start choosing work that actually means something to them," Tsai said.

Not everyone is convinced. Some students argue that long-term placements are difficult to fit around part-time jobs and lab schedules. "I support the idea, but I work twenty hours a week," said Jason Lee, a junior in electrical engineering. "Weekend-only options are limited." In response, the center plans to expand online volunteering, such as remote tutoring for rural schools, starting next spring.
For many participants, though, the benefits are clear. "At first I just wanted the hours," said Amy Lin, a sophomore who tutors at a senior center. "Now I visit even when I don't need to."

questions.explain: 全文從「只為湊時數」談到調查顯示學生態度轉變及其原因，選 C。時數一直是 36 小時，並未增加（A 錯）。
options: Why the university increased the required service hours
A new scholarship for student volunteers
How students' attitudes toward service learning have changed
Problems at a local senior center
questions.prompt: What is the article mainly about?

questions.explain: Tsai 說學生必須說明學到什麼時，就會選擇對自己有意義的服務，選 B。報告是新增的要求，並未取代時數（C 錯）。
options: It is too difficult for most students
It encourages students to choose more meaningful service
It is required only for one-time events

options: To show that he has already finished his hours

options: A limit on hours from one-time events
